Madaniyya (Medinan), and it has twelve verses, two hundred and forty-seven words, and one thousand and sixty letters.

Ibn al-Muqri informed me: Ibn Mațar informed us: Ibn Shuwayk narrated to us: Ibn Yunus narrated to us: Sallam ibn Sulaym narrated to us: Harun ibn Kathir narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umama al-Bahili, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the surah 'O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you' will be given by Allah a sincere repentance (tawbatan nasuhan)" [335] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/52.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

The reason for its revelation: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to, when he prayed the morning prayer, enter upon his wives one by one. Hafsah bint Umar had been given a pot of honey, and whenever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon her, she would detain him and give him to drink from it. 'A'isha disliked his staying long with her, so she said to a Abyssinian slave-girl of hers called Hasan: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) enters upon Hafsah, go in to her and observe what he does." So she informed her of the news and of the matter of the honey. 'A'isha became jealous and sent to her companions (co-wives), informing them, and said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) enters upon you, say: 'We find the smell of maghafir on you'," which is the gum of the 'urfut tree, foul in smell, and the Messenger of Allah disliked it.

He said: The Messenger entered upon Sawda. She said: "I did not want to say that to the Messenger of Allah, but then I feared 'A'isha, so I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is this smell I find from you? Did you eat maghafir?'"

He said: "No, but Hafsah gave me honey to drink." Then the Messenger entered upon each of his wives one by one, and they all said to him the same. Then he entered upon 'A'isha, and she covered her nose. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to her: "What is the matter with you?" She said: "I smell the odor of maghafir. Did you eat it, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "No, rather Hafsah gave me honey to drink."

She said: "Perhaps her bees had fed on 'urfut." He said to her (ﷺ): "By Allah, I will never drink it again," and he made it forbidden to himself [336] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/178; Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/55.]].

'Ata' ibn Abi Muslim said: The one who used to give the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to drink was Umm Salama.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us: Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad al-A'war narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj who said: 'Ata' claimed that he heard 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr say: I heard 'A'isha, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), may Allah be pleased with her, relate that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to stay with Zaynab bint Jahsh and drink honey with her. She said: So I and Hafsah agreed that whichever of us the Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon, she would say:

"I find the smell of maghafir from you." He entered upon one of them and she said that to him, and he said: "No, rather I drank honey at the house of Zaynab bint Jahsh, and I will not return to it." Then the verses "O Prophet, why do you forbid..." were revealed [337] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/177.]].

They said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had divided the days among his wives. When it was Hafsah's day, she said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have a need to my father, a provision of mine with him; permit me to visit him." He permitted her. When she went out, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for his slave-girl Maria the Copt, Umm Ibrahim, whom al-Muqawqis had given him, and brought her into Hafsah's house and had intercourse with her. Hafsah came and found the door locked, so she was kept waiting at the door. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) came out with his face dripping with sweat, and Hafsah was weeping. He said: "What makes you weep?" She said: "You only permitted me for this: you brought your slave-girl into my house, and then you had intercourse with her on my day and on my bed. Did you not see any respect and right for me? Would you do this with any of your other wives?" The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Is she not my slave-girl whom Allah has made lawful for me? Be silent. She is forbidden to me, seeking thereby your approval. Do not tell any of the other women about this; it is a trust with you" [338] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 5/9.]].

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out, Hafsah knocked on the wall between her and 'A'isha and said: "Shall I not give you good news? The Messenger of Allah has forbidden Maria to himself; Allah has relieved us of her." Then she informed 'A'isha of what she had seen. They were close friends and allies against the rest of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ). 'A'isha became angry and kept at the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) until he swore that he would not approach her. So Allah revealed: "O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you" — meaning the honey and Maria.

'Ikrima said: It was revealed concerning the woman who gave herself to the Prophet (peace be upon him), who is called Umm Sharik, but the Prophet (peace be upon him) refused to accept her, for the sake of his wife: "seeking the approval of your wives. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."

Al-Kalbi said: He confided to her that your father and the father of 'A'isha would be two caliphs over my community after me.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, reading to him: Umar ibn al-Hasan informed us: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Sa'id narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Husayn narrated to us, from al-Hurr al-Muslli, from Khalaf ibn Abi Thabit, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement" — he said: The Prophet (ﷺ) confided the matter of the caliphate after him, and Hafsah related it.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Nasr ibn Muhammad ibn Shirzad informed us: al-Hasan ibn Sa'id al-Bazzar narrated to us: Khalid ibn al-Awwam al-Bazzar narrated to us: Furat ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to me, from Maymun ibn Mihran concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted, "And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement," he said: He confided to her that Abu Bakr would be my caliph after me.

﴿So when she informed [of it]﴾ — she informed her companion of the statement the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had confided to her.

﴿And Allah disclosed it to him﴾ — i.e., Allah informed His Prophet (ﷺ) that she had informed of it.

Talha ibn Musarrif recited: "fa-lamma anba'at bihi" with the alif.

﴿He made known part of it﴾ — 'Ali, Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatada and al-Kisa'i recited it: "'arrafa" with the light form (tashdid absent).

Muhammad ibn Abdus informed us: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-Jahm narrated to us: al-Farra' narrated to us: a shaykh of the Banu Asad, meaning al-Kisa'i, narrated to me, from Nu'aym ibn 'Amr, from 'Ata', from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: When a man recited to him "'arrafa" with the doubled form, he would pelt him with pebbles. Its meaning on this reading: "He made known part of it" — what she had done of disclosing his secret — i.e., he was angry with her for it and repaid her, from the saying of one who says to someone who has wronged him: "La-u'arrifanna laka" meaning "I will certainly repay you for it."

They said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) repaid her by divorcing her, but when this reached 'Umar, he said: "If there were any good in the family of 'Umar, the Messenger of Allah would not have divorced you for a month." Then Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him and ordered him to take her back. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) withdrew from his wives for a month and sat in the upper chamber of Umm Ibrahim Maria, until the verse of choice was revealed. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not divorce Hafsah; he had only intended to divorce her, but Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him and said: "Do not divorce her, for she is fasting often and praying often, and she is one of your wives in Paradise," so he did not divorce her.

The rest recited "'arrafa" with the doubled form, meaning: he informed Hafsah of part of that statement and told her of it. This was chosen by Abu Hatim and Abu 'Ubayda, who said: "Because in the exegesis it is that he informed her of part of what she had said, and what confirms this is His saying: ﴿and turned away from part﴾, meaning he did not inform her of it and did not tell her of it. If 'arrafa bA'ḍahu were the light form, its opposite would be 'anakara ba'ḍan (he denied part), and He would not have said a'raḍa 'anhu (he turned away from it)."

Al-Hasan said: A generous person never fully probes; Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He made known part of it and turned away from part.﴾

Muqatil said: It means he informed her of part of what he had said to 'A'isha, and did not tell her all of her words; he made Hafsah know part and turned away from part of the statement that Abu Bakr and 'Umar would rule after me.

﴿So when he informed her of it﴾ — i.e., he informed Hafsah of what Allah had disclosed to him.

﴿She said: "Who told you this?" He said: "The All-Knowing, the All-Aware informed me."﴾

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Nasr ibn Muhammad ibn Shirzad informed us: al-Hasan ibn Sa'id al-Bazzar narrated to us: Khalid ibn al-Awwam al-Bazzar narrated to us: Furat ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to me, from Maymun ibn Mihran concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted, "And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement," he said: He confided to her that Abu Bakr would be my caliph after me.

﴿So when she informed [of it]﴾ — she informed her companion of the statement the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had confided to her.

﴿And Allah disclosed it to him﴾ — i.e., Allah informed His Prophet (ﷺ) that she had informed of it.

Talha ibn Musarrif recited: "fa-lamma anba'at bihi" with the alif.

﴿He made known part of it﴾ — 'Ali, Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatada and al-Kisa'i recited it: "'arrafa" with the light form (tashdid absent).

Muhammad ibn Abdus informed us: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-Jahm narrated to us: al-Farra' narrated to us: a shaykh of the Banu Asad, meaning al-Kisa'i, narrated to me, from Nu'aym ibn 'Amr, from 'Ata', from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: When a man recited to him "'arrafa" with the doubled form, he would pelt him with pebbles. Its meaning on this reading: "He made known part of it" — what she had done of disclosing his secret — i.e., he was angry with her for it and repaid her, from the saying of one who says to someone who has wronged him: "La-u'arrifanna laka" meaning "I will certainly repay you for it."

They said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) repaid her by divorcing her, but when this reached 'Umar, he said: "If there were any good in the family of 'Umar, the Messenger of Allah would not have divorced you for a month." Then Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him and ordered him to take her back. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) withdrew from his wives for a month and sat in the upper chamber of Umm Ibrahim Maria, until the verse of choice was revealed. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not divorce Hafsah; he had only intended to divorce her, but Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him and said: "Do not divorce her, for she is fasting often and praying often, and she is one of your wives in Paradise," so he did not divorce her.

The rest recited "'arrafa" with the doubled form, meaning: he informed Hafsah of part of that statement and told her of it. This was chosen by Abu Hatim and Abu 'Ubayda, who said: "Because in the exegesis it is that he informed her of part of what she had said, and what confirms this is His saying: ﴿and turned away from part﴾, meaning he did not inform her of it and did not tell her of it. If 'arrafa bA'ḍahu were the light form, its opposite would be 'anakara ba'ḍan (he denied part), and He would not have said a'raḍa 'anhu (he turned away from it)."

Al-Hasan said: A generous person never fully probes; Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He made known part of it and turned away from part.﴾

Muqatil said: It means he informed her of part of what he had said to 'A'isha, and did not tell her all of her words; he made Hafsah know part and turned away from part of the statement that Abu Bakr and 'Umar would rule after me.

﴿So when he informed her of it﴾ — i.e., he informed Hafsah of what Allah had disclosed to him.

﴿She said: "Who told you this?" He said: "The All-Knowing, the All-Aware informed me."﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 66, verse 4:

﴿If you two turn in repentance to Allah, then your hearts have indeed inclined,﴾ meaning: deviated and leaned away, and you have deserved repentance.

Ibn Zayd said: "Their hearts inclined in that it pleased them that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would abstain from his slave-girl, and that was agreeable to them, so they opposed what the Messenger of Allah disliked."

Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Hamdun informed us, reading to him: Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Thawr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "I had always been eager to ask Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) about the two wives of the Messenger of Allah concerning whom Allah the Exalted said: ﴿If you two turn in repentance to Allah, then your hearts have indeed inclined﴾, until Umar performed the pilgrimage and I performed it with him. When we were on part of the road, Umar turned aside and I turned aside with him carrying the water-vessel. He relieved himself, then came to me and I poured water over his hands, and he performed ablution. I said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, who are the two wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning whom Allah the Exalted said: ﴿If you two turn in repentance to Allah, then your hearts have indeed inclined﴾?' Umar said: 'Wonderful, you, O son of Abbas!'"

al-Zuhri said: "He disliked what he was asked, and did not conceal it. Then he said: 'They are Hafsa and Aisha.' Then he began to narrate the hadith, saying: 'We, the people of Quraysh, were a people who dominated women. When we came to Madina, we found a people whose women dominated them, so our women began to learn from their women.'"

He said: "My dwelling was among the Banu Umayya ibn Zayd in al-Awali." He said: "One day I became angry with my wife, and she began to argue back at me. I disapproved that she should argue with me, and she said: 'Why is it disapproved that I argue with you? By Allah, the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) do argue with him, and one of them abandons him from day until night.'" He said: "So I set out and entered upon Hafsa and said: 'Do you argue with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?' She said: 'Yes.' I said: 'And does one of you abandon him from day until night?' She said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Then he among you who does that has failed and lost. Are any of you secure that Allah will not be angry with her because of the anger of His Messenger (ﷺ), and then she will be destroyed?

Do not argue with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), do not ask him anything, and ask me whatever you wish. Do not let it deceive you if your neighbour is more beautiful and more beloved to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) than you'—meaning Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her)."

He said: "I had a neighbour from the Ansar. We would take turns going down to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him): he would go down one day and I the next, and he would bring me news of the revelation and other matters, and I would bring him the same. We used to say that the Ghassanids were preparing horses to attack us. One day my companion went down, then came to me in the evening and knocked on my door, then called me. I came out to him and he said: 'A great matter has occurred.'

I said: 'What is it? Have the Ghassanids come?' He said: 'Greater than that! The Messenger has divorced his wives.' I said: 'Hafsa has failed and lost. I had been thinking this would happen.' When I had prayed the dawn prayer, I tightened my garments and went down, and entered upon Hafsa while she was weeping. I said: 'Has the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divorced you?' She said: 'I do not know. He is secluded in this upper room.' So I came to his black servant and said: 'Ask permission for Umar.' The servant entered, then came out to me and said: 'I mentioned you to him, but he remained silent.' So I went off until I came to the pulpit, and around it were a group of people sitting, some of them weeping. I sat a little, then what I felt overcame me, so I came to the servant and said: 'Ask permission for Umar.' He entered, then came out to me and said: 'I mentioned you to him, but he remained silent.' So I went out and sat by the pulpit, then what I felt overcame me again, so I came to the servant—meaning the servant—and said: 'Ask permission for Umar.' He entered, then came out to me and said: 'I mentioned you to him, but he remained silent.' He said: 'I turned to leave, and the servant called me and said: "Enter, for he has given you permission."' So I entered and greeted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he was reclining on a mat of palm fibre which had left its mark on his side. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, have you divorced your wives?' He raised his head to me and said: 'No.'

I said: 'Allahu akbar!' Then I related to him what I had said to my wife and what she had said to me. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) smiled. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, Hafsa came in to me and I mentioned to her what I had said.' He smiled again. I said: 'Shall I seek permission to remain, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Yes.' So I sat down and raised my head to look at the room, and by Allah I saw nothing in it that catches the eye except three hides. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, ask Allah the Exalted to widen provision for your community, for He has widened it for Persia and Byzantium, and they do not worship Allah.' He sat up straight and said: '"Or are you in doubt, O son of al-Khattab? Those have had their good things hastened for them in the life of this world."' [339] I said: 'Ask forgiveness for me, O Messenger of Allah.' He had sworn not to enter upon them for a month, out of his great displeasure with them, until Allah the Exalted rebuked him."

al-Zuhri said: "Urwa informed me from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: 'When twenty-nine nights had passed over the Messenger of Allah, he came to me first, and I said: "O Messenger of Allah, you swore that you would not enter upon us for a month, and you have entered upon me after twenty-nine. I am counting them." He said: "The month is twenty-nine." Then he said: "O Aisha, I am going to mention a matter to you, and there is no harm in you not hastening in it until you consult your two parents."' She said: 'Then he recited to me: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives…﴾ until ﴿a great reward﴾.' Aisha said: 'He knew that my parents would not command me—and it was said: "would command me to part from him"—so I said: "Shall I consult my parents about this? Rather I desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode."'

Aisha said: 'I said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, do not tell your wives that I chose you."' He said: 'The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah sent me only as a conveyor of the message, and did not send me as one who imposes hardship."' [340] [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 5/96, no. 3374.]]

﴿And if you back one another against him﴾, meaning: support one another in harming the Prophet (ﷺ). The people of Kufa recited it with the ẓā' lightened (taẓāharā), by elision, and Abu Ubayd preferred this; the rest recited it with doubling (tazẓāharā), by assimilation, and Abu Hatim preferred this.

﴿then indeed Allah is his protector﴾, meaning: his guardian (walī), protector and helper.

﴿and Gabriel and the righteous among the believers﴾. al-Musayyib ibn Shurayk said: "It is Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him)."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Umar (may Allah be pleased with him)." Ikrima said: "Abu Bakr and Umar." What supports this is what Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Nasrawayh narrated to us: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Sulayman al-Baqillani narrated to us: Abu Ammar al-Husayn ibn al-Harith narrated to us: Abd al-Rahim ibn Zayd al-Ammi narrated to us, from his father, from Suqayq, from Abd Allah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Allah is his protector, and Gabriel and the righteous among the believers﴾. He said: "Indeed the righteous among the believers are Abu Bakr and Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both)." [341] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/127.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abu Ali al-Muqri narrated to us: Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Abi Umar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, a trustworthy man raising it to Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said concerning Allah's saying: "the righteous among the believers is Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)." [342] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/189; Shawahid al-Tanzil: 2/341.]]

Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us: Umar ibn al-Hasan informed us: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Husayn narrated to us, from Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers, from Asma bint Umays, who said: "I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: 'The righteous among the believers is Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him).'" [343] [[Fath al-Bari: 10/353.]]

al-Kalbi said: "They are the sincere ones who are not hypocrites."

Qatada and al-'Ala' ibn Ziyad al-'Adawi said: "They are the prophets."

﴿and the angels after that are a supporting company﴾, meaning: helpers. He did not say "ṣāliḥū" nor "ẓuhr," because although the word of each is singular, it carries the sense of the plural, as when a man says: "None recites to me except a reciter of the Qur'an," which is singular in form but plural in meaning, since he has permitted every reciter of the Qur'an to recite to him.

﴿It may be that if he divorces you, his Lord will give him in exchange wives better than you: submissive, faithful, devout, obedient, repentant, worshipful, who fast, previously married and virgins.﴾ It was said: "obedient" means those who pray.

﴿Repentant, worshipful, wandering (in devotion)﴾, who will go along with him wherever he goes. It was said: "fasting."

Zayd ibn Aslam, his son, and Yaman said: "emigrants."

﴿Previously married and virgins.﴾ The verse is given as a report about capability, not about what is actually occurring at the time, because He, exalted is He, said: ﴿if he divorces you﴾ while He knew that he would not divorce them. This is His statement: ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be like you﴾. This is a report about capability and a warning to them, not that there is anyone in existence better than the Community of Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿O you who believe, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are angels, harsh and severe, who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them and do what they are commanded.﴾ Meaning: command them to do good, forbid them from evil, teach them, and bring them close to piety; that is their protection from the Fire. Its guards are severe and strong, meaning mighty, in whom Allah has not placed mercy. They are the nineteen guardians (zabaniyah, the angels of punishment) and their helpers from the keepers of the Fire.

﴿They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded.﴾

﴿O you who disbelieve, do not make excuses today; you are only being recompensed for what you used to do.﴾

﴿O you who believe, turn to Allah in sincere repentance.﴾ The common reading is with a fatha on the nūn, as an attribute of repentance.

Hammad and Yahya ibn Adam narrated from Abu Bakr, from ʿĀṣim, with a ḍamma on it, as a verbal noun, and this is the reading of al-Hasan.

Al-Mubarrad said: He intended "repentance that possesses sincerity." The exegetes differed on the meaning of "sincere repentance."

ʿUmar, Ubayy, and Muʿādh said: Sincere repentance is that one repents and then does not return to the sin, just as milk does not return to the udder. Muʿādh raised this to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Al-Hasan said: It is that the servant is regretful for what has passed and resolved never to return to it.

Al-Kalbī said: It is that one seeks forgiveness with the tongue, regrets with the heart, and refrains with the body.

Qatādah said: It is that which is truthful and sincere.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: It is an accepted repentance, and it is not accepted unless three things are present in it: fear that it will not be accepted, hope that it will be accepted, and persistence in acts of obedience.

Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said: It is a repentance by which you counsel your own selves.

Al-Qurzī said: Four things comprise it: seeking forgiveness with the tongue, abandoning sin with the body, showing the intention not to return in the heart, and leaving bad companions.

Sufyān al-Thawrī said: The sign of sincere repentance is four: scarcity (of food), sickness, humility, and strangeness (estrangement from people).

Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ said: It is that the sin remains before one's eyes, and one continues as if looking at it.

Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Wāsiṭī said: It is a repentance not for the sake of a reward, because whoever sins in this world for the comfort of his soul, and then repents seeking its comfort in the Hereafter, his repentance is for the share of his own soul and not for Allah.

Abū Bakr al-Warrāq said: It is that the earth becomes constricting for you despite its vastness, and your own self becomes constricting for you, like the repentance of "the three who were left behind."

Abū Bakr al-Raqqāq al-Miṣrī said: Returning wrongs, seeking the pardon of adversaries, and persistence in acts of obedience.

Ruwaym al-Rāʿī said: It is that you be for Allah a face without a back, just as you were to Him, when in sin, a back without a face.

Rābiʿa said: A repentance from which there is no return.

Dhū al-Nūn said: Its signs are three: little speech, little food, and little sleep.

Suqayq said: It is that its possessor greatly blames his own self and never ceases to regret, so that he may be saved from its afflictions by safety.

Sarī al-Saqaṭī said: Sincere repentance is not valid except by counseling the believers regarding oneself, because among the soundness of one's repentance is that one loves for people to be like oneself.

Al-Junayd said: It is that one forgets the sin so that one never mentions it again, because among the soundness of one's repentance is that one becomes a lover of Allah, and whoever loves Allah forgets what is other than Allah.

Sahl said: It is the repentance of the People of the Sunnah and the Community, because the innovator has no repentance, based on the statement of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Allah has forbidden every possessor of innovation from repenting."

Abū al-Adyān said: It is that its possessor has flowing tears and a heart gathered away from sins. When that is so, his repentance is sincere, and the signs of his repentance appear.

Fatḥ al-Mawṣilī said: Its signs are three: opposing the desire (of the self), much weeping, and enduring hunger and thirst.

﴿It may be that your Lord will expiate your sins from you and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow, on the day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him. Their light will run before them and on their right, on the Bridge (al-Ṣirāt).﴾

﴿They will say, when the light of the hypocrites is extinguished:﴾ ﴿Our Lord, complete for us our light and forgive us; indeed You are over all things competent.﴾

﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be stern with them; their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.﴾

Then He gave an example of the righteous women, and the righteous among women. So the Mighty One, Majestic, said: ﴿Allah presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot.﴾ The name of Noah's wife was Wāghilah, and the wife of Lot was named Wāhilah. Muqātil said: "al-ʿAduww" and "al-Wahilah."

﴿They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them, and the two husbands could not avail them against Allah at all; and it was said: "Enter the Fire with those who enter."﴾ Their betrayal was not in adultery; rather, their betrayal was that they were upon a religion other than theirs. Noah's wife would tell the people that he was mad and would inform on his secrets; whenever anyone believed in Noah, she would inform the tyrants of Noah's people about him. As for Lot's wife, she would direct his people to his guests.

﴿But they availed them nothing against Allah, and it was said: "Enter the Fire with those who enter."﴾ This warns ʿĀʾishah and Ḥafṣah, may Allah be pleased with them both.

﴿Allah presents an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh﴾, who was Āsiyah bint Muzāḥim.

The exegetes said: When Moses overcame the magicians, the wife of Pharaoh believed. When her Islam became clear and she remained steadfast upon it, he staked her hands and feet with four stakes, cast her into the sun, and ordered a great rock to be dropped upon her. When they brought the rock, she said: ﴿My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise﴾, and she saw her house in Paradise made of pearl. Allah took her soul, and the rock was dropped upon a body with no spirit in it, so she did not feel the pain of Pharaoh's torment.

Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Kaysān said: Allah raised the wife of Pharaoh to Paradise, and she is in it, eating and drinking.

We were told by Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥamdūn, who was told by ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdān, who was told by Abū al-Azhar, who was told by Asbāṭ, from Sulaymān, from Abū ʿUthmān, from Salmān, who said: The wife of Pharaoh was tormented by the sun, and when they departed from her, the angels would shade her, and she would see her house in Paradise.

﴿And deliver me from Pharaoh and his deed﴾, meaning his religion.

We were told by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid, who was told by Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Saʿīd, who was told by ʿAlī ibn Ḥarth, who was told by Abū al-Mundhir Hishām ibn Muḥammad, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding Allah's statement: ﴿And deliver me from Pharaoh and his deed, and deliver me from the wrongdoing people﴾, meaning the disbelievers. By this verse Allah cut off the hope of one who commits disobedience and hopes that the righteousness of another will benefit him, and He informed that the disobedience of another does not harm him when he is obedient.

﴿And Mary, daughter of ʿImrān, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into it of Our spirit﴾, meaning into her garment; for this reason the pronoun is used.

﴿And she affirmed﴾: the common reading is with the emphatic doubling; Lāḥiq ibn Ḥumayd read it without doubling.

﴿The words of her Lord﴾: the common reading is in the plural.

Al-Ḥasan, ʿĪsā, and al-Jaḥdarī read "the word" in the singular, meaning ʿĪsā (peace be upon him).

﴿And His books﴾: Abū ʿAmr and Yaʿqūb read "wa-kutubihi" in the plural, and it is the transmission of Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim and the choice of Abū Ḥātim, who said: "Because it is more general."

The rest read "wa-kitābihi" in the singular, and this is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd.

﴿And she was among the obedient﴾, meaning the obedient ones. Its implication is: from the devout people; for this reason it did not say "obedient women," similar to ﴿O Mary, be obedient to your Lord﴾.

We were told by al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad, who was told by Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq al-Sunnī and Muḥammad ibn al-Muẓaffar, who said: ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Sulaymān told us, Mūsā ibn Sābiq told us, Ibn Wahb told us, al-Māḍī ibn Muḥammad informed me, from Bardah, from Makḥūl, from Muʿādh ibn Jabal: that the Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon Khadījah while she was giving up her soul, and he said: "I dislike what has befallen you, O Khadījah, and Allah has placed in what is disliked much good. When you come to your co-wives, convey my greetings to them."

She said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are they?"

He said: "Mary daughter of ʿImrān, Āsiyah daughter of Muzāḥim, and Kulthūm or Ḥalīmah, sister of Moses." The narrator was uncertain. She said: "With comfort and sons."

We were told by al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad, who was told by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Shaybah, who was told by ʿUbayd Allāh Aḥmad ibn Manṣūr al-Kisā'ī, who was told by Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār known as Sandūl al-Hamadānī, who was told by Abū Usāmah, from Shuʿbah, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Abū Mūsā, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Many men have reached perfection, but none of the women have reached perfection except four: Āsiyah daughter of Muzāḥim, the wife of Pharaoh; Mary daughter of ʿImrān; Khadījah daughter of Khuwaylid; and Fāṭimah daughter of Muḥammad. And the superiority of ʿĀʾishah over the women is like the superiority of tharīd over all other food."

﴿It may be that if he divorces you, his Lord will give him in exchange wives better than you: submissive, faithful, devout, obedient, repentant, worshipful, who fast, previously married and virgins.﴾ It was said: "obedient" means those who pray.

﴿Repentant, worshipful, wandering (in devotion)﴾, who will go along with him wherever he goes. It was said: "fasting."

Zayd ibn Aslam, his son, and Yaman said: "emigrants."

﴿Previously married and virgins.﴾ The verse is given as a report about capability, not about what is actually occurring at the time, because He, exalted is He, said: ﴿if he divorces you﴾ while He knew that he would not divorce them. This is His statement: ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be like you﴾. This is a report about capability and a warning to them, not that there is anyone in existence better than the Community of Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿O you who believe, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are angels, harsh and severe, who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them and do what they are commanded.﴾ Meaning: command them to do good, forbid them from evil, teach them, and bring them close to piety; that is their protection from the Fire. Its guards are severe and strong, meaning mighty, in whom Allah has not placed mercy. They are the nineteen guardians (zabaniyah, the angels of punishment) and their helpers from the keepers of the Fire.

﴿They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded.﴾

﴿O you who disbelieve, do not make excuses today; you are only being recompensed for what you used to do.﴾

﴿O you who believe, turn to Allah in sincere repentance.﴾ The common reading is with a fatha on the nūn, as an attribute of repentance.

Hammad and Yahya ibn Adam narrated from Abu Bakr, from ʿĀṣim, with a ḍamma on it, as a verbal noun, and this is the reading of al-Hasan.

Al-Mubarrad said: He intended "repentance that possesses sincerity." The exegetes differed on the meaning of "sincere repentance."

ʿUmar, Ubayy, and Muʿādh said: Sincere repentance is that one repents and then does not return to the sin, just as milk does not return to the udder. Muʿādh raised this to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said: It is a repentance by which you counsel your own selves.

Al-Qurzī said: Four things comprise it: seeking forgiveness with the tongue, abandoning sin with the body, showing the intention not to return in the heart, and leaving bad companions.

Sufyān al-Thawrī said: The sign of sincere repentance is four: scarcity (of food), sickness, humility, and strangeness (estrangement from people).

Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ said: It is that the sin remains before one's eyes, and one continues as if looking at it.

Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Wāsiṭī said: It is a repentance not for the sake of a reward, because whoever sins in this world for the comfort of his soul, and then repents seeking its comfort in the Hereafter, his repentance is for the share of his own soul and not for Allah.

Ruwaym al-Rāʿī said: It is that you be for Allah a face without a back, just as you were to Him, when in sin, a back without a face.

Rābiʿa said: A repentance from which there is no return.

Suqayq said: It is that its possessor greatly blames his own self and never ceases to regret, so that he may be saved from its afflictions by safety.

Al-Hasan said: It is that the servant is regretful for what has passed and resolved never to return to it.

Al-Kalbī said: It is that one seeks forgiveness with the tongue, regrets with the heart, and refrains with the body.

Qatādah said: It is that which is truthful and sincere.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: It is an accepted repentance, and it is not accepted unless three things are present in it: fear that it will not be accepted, hope that it will be accepted, and persistence in acts of obedience.

Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said: It is a repentance by which you counsel your own selves.

Al-Qurzī said: Four things comprise it: seeking forgiveness with the tongue, abandoning sin with the body, showing the intention not to return in the heart, and leaving bad companions.

Sufyān al-Thawrī said: The sign of sincere repentance is four: scarcity (of food), sickness, humility, and strangeness (estrangement from people).

Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ said: It is that the sin remains before one's eyes, and one continues as if looking at it.

Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Wāsiṭī said: It is a repentance not for the sake of a reward, because whoever sins in this world for the comfort of his soul, and then repents seeking its comfort in the Hereafter, his repentance is for the share of his own soul and not for Allah.

Abū Bakr al-Raqqāq al-Miṣrī said: Returning wrongs, seeking the pardon of adversaries, and persistence in acts of obedience.

Ruwaym al-Rāʿī said: It is that you be for Allah a face without a back, just as you were to Him, when in sin, a back without a face.

Rābiʿa said: A repentance from which there is no return.

Dhū al-Nūn said: Its signs are three: little speech, little food, and little sleep.

Suqayq said: It is that its possessor greatly blames his own self and never ceases to regret, so that he may be saved from its afflictions by safety.

Sarī al-Saqaṭī said: Sincere repentance is not valid except by counseling the believers regarding oneself, because among the soundness of one's repentance is that one loves for people to be like oneself.

Al-Junayd said: It is that one forgets the sin so that one never mentions it again, because among the soundness of one's repentance is that one becomes a lover of Allah, and whoever loves Allah forgets what is other than Allah.

Sahl said: It is the repentance of the People of the Sunnah and the Community, because the innovator has no repentance, based on the statement of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Allah has forbidden every possessor of innovation from repenting."

Abū al-Adyān said: It is that its possessor has flowing tears and a heart gathered away from sins. When that is so, his repentance is sincere, and the signs of his repentance appear.

Fatḥ al-Mawṣilī said: Its signs are three: opposing the desire (of the self), much weeping, and enduring hunger and thirst.
